Definition: a pit (especially as a trap); figuratively, destruction
BiblicalUsage: The pit is the Bible's picture of the grave as a trap, a hole dug to catch the unwary. The psalmist trusts that God will not leave his soul in hell nor suffer His Holy One to see corruption, while Hezekiah praises the God who delivered his soul from the pit of corruption and cast all his sins behind His back. Elihu promises the same rescue, that God will deliver the soul from going into the pit and its life shall see the light.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the pit is the end of every road that leads away from God, and only God can pull a person out of it. The promise that His Holy One would not see corruption is the promise that the pit does not get the last word.
